world.bio: I edit other people's documentaries for a living, mostly for PBS affiliates and small streaming outfits. I have cut thirty-one films in fifteen years, two of them shortlisted at festivals. Ten years ago I shot sixty hours of interviews with Chinatown elders for a film of my own. It was never funded. The tapes are in a closet in my Sunset Park apartment. I coach my son's Little League team and I am learning to bake sourdough.
skills_assets: Avid and Premiere editing; fifteen years of narrative structure work on documentaries
Sixty hours of interviews with Chinatown elders, shot on a Panasonic DVX100 and a Canon 5D over 2015-2016, digitised to a 4 TB drive
A Rolodex of grant writers, festival programmers and archivists
English and passable Cantonese; my parents spoke Toisan at home, I understand it but I do not speak it
A cut-room in the back of a friend's studio in Gowanus, rented for 200 dollars a month

projects.name: The Elders, unfinished
projects.text: Ten years ago I interviewed forty-two people in Chinatown, aged 70 to 95, about their journeys and their working lives in laundries, restaurants and garment shops. Many of them spoke Cantonese, a few spoke Taishanese. Two of the interviewees have died since. The film stalled because two transcription services gave up on the Taishanese passages, and a third said they could not tell which parts were Cantonese and which were Taishanese. Without a transcript I cannot structure the cut, and without a structure I cannot apply for a grant.

projects.name: Client work: a 60-minute film on a Bronx bakery
projects.text: I am the lead editor on a film about a family bakery. Rough cut due on 20 October.

projects.name: Little League fall season
projects.text: Coaching nine-year-olds. We are 3 and 4. I make them run laps when they sulk.

notes.text: Bakery film: client wants more shots of dough. I told her the audience wants faces. She said, dough is a face. Annoying.
Opened the closet and looked at the stack of tapes. The label says 'Mr. Chen, laundry, 2015'. The 4 TB drive has all of them. I have not touched it in two years.
Rent-stabilised lease renewal came: 2.75 percent increase. Told my wife we will stay another year. She sighed and said at least it is not 10 percent.
Sourdough starter died again. I fed it every day for a week then forgot over a weekend. My son said it is called Gerald and it deserved better.

Thinking about the Chinatown film. Last time I tried to get it transcribed the service sent back pages with [inaudible] every ten seconds. The worst part was the elder who talked about the boat journey in Taishanese, his voice breaking. I could understand about a third. I felt like I was stealing his story by not being able to read it.
A grant program deadline is in March. I have a short list of what I need: a sample cut of twenty minutes, a treatment, a transcript. The transcript is the problem.
Little League game: lost 8-2. After the game, one of the kids asked, Coach Dan, why do you always bring snacks even when we lose? I said because we are a team.
My mother called from Queens. She asked what I am working on. I said a bakery film. She said what about the old people. I changed the subject.
Film fund email: no news. I keep opening my email as if it is a lottery.

messages.text:
Client: Can we get the dough scene up front?
Me: We can try. The audience may not connect unless there is a person on screen early.
Client: The baker's hands are a person.

Jen: Did you pay the electric bill?
Me: Yes, yesterday.
Jen: And the rent?
Me: Next week.

Marco: Any chance you finish the Chinatown film this year?
Me: Not unless I find someone to transcribe the Taishanese.
Marco: You will find someone.

Mother: Come to dinner Sunday. I will make jook.
Me: I will bring the kids.
Mother: Bring the old tapes, I want to see them.

relations.about: Public-school teacher; supportive but tired of the unfinished film.
Plays outfield, loves Gerald the sourdough.
Lives in Flushing, speaks Toisan, remembers the old neighbourhood.

constraints: Cannot take full-time jobs; must be flexible for school pickup
Needs a transcript before applying for any grant
Will not release interviews without family consent of the elders
sensitive: Savings are low; living on freelance checks that arrive 60 days late
Two of the interviewees have died and he feels he owes them the film
